source_text: Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ τοῖς γεγαμηκόσι παραινέσαιμι ἂν οἴκοι τὰς γυναῖκας τὰς σφῶν μήποτε κατὰ πρόσωπον οἰκετῶν φιλεῖν. οὐδὲ γὰρ προσγελᾶν δούλοις Ἀριστοτέλης εἴα ποτέ, πολλοῦ γε καὶ δεῖ κατ᾿ ὄψιν αὐτῶν φιλοφρονούμενον φαίνεσθαι τὴν γυναῖκα. ἄμεινον δὲ οἴκοθεν ἀρξαμένους ἀπὸ τοῦ γάμου τὴν σεμνότητα ἐπιδείκνυσθαι. μεγίστη γὰρ ἡ σωφροσύνης συζυγία καθαρᾶς ἡδονῆς ἀποπνέουσα. πάνυ γοῦν θαυμασίως ἡ τραγῳδία. φεῦ φεῦ, γυναῖκες, (φησίν) ὡς ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἄρα οὐ χρυσός, οὐ τυραννίς, οὐ πλούτου χλιδὴ τοσοῦτον εἶχε διαφόρους τὰς ἡδονὰς ὡς ἀνδρὸς ἐσθλοῦ καὶ γυναικὸς εὐσεβοῦς γνώμη δικαία καὶ φρονοῦσα τἄνδικα. ταῦτα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τὰ παραγγέλματα καὶ παρὰ τοῖς τὴν κοσμικὴν μετιοῦσι σοφίαν ἐκφωνηθέντα οὐ παραιτητέον. ἐγνωκότες οὖν »τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον, ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε, εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἐλυτρώθημεν ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ἡμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου, ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ.« »ἀρκετὸς οὖν ὁ παρεληλυθὼς χρόνος,« ὁ Πέτρος φησί, »τὸ βούλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν κατειργάσθαι, πεπορευμένους ἐν ἀσελγείαις, ἐπιθυμίαις, οἰνοφλυγίαις, κώμοις, πότοις καὶ ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρείαις.« ὅρον ἔχωμεν τὸν σταυρὸν τοῦ κυρίου, ᾧ περισταυρούμεθα καὶ περιθριγκούμεθα τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν. ἀναγεννηθέντες τοίνυν προσηλωθῶμεν [ἐν] τῇ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀνανήψωμέν τε καὶ ἁγιασθῶμεν, »ὅτι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν, πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά. καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ἡμᾶς, ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ζηλωταὶ γενώμεθα;« ἡ δὲ ἀρίστη ἀγωγὴ εὐταξία ἐστίν, παντελὴς οὖσα εὐσχημοσύνη καὶ δύναμις τεταγμένη βεβαία, τῶν ἑξῆς ἀλλήλοις κειμένων ἐν ἔργῳ καλῶς ἀποδοτική, κατ᾿ ἀρετὴν ἀνυπέρβλητος. Ταῦτα, εἰ καὶ τραχύτερον προηνέχθην οἰκονομούμενος τῆς ἐπανορθώσεως τὴν σωτηρίαν, ἐμοὶ μὲν λελέχθων, φησὶν ὁ παιδαγωγός, ἐπειδὴ »ὁ ἐλέγχων μετὰ παρρησίας εἰρηνοποιεῖ,« ὑμεῖς δὲ εἰ μὲν ἀκούσεσθέ μου, σωθήσεσθε, εἰ δ᾿ οὐ προσέξετε τοῖς εἰρημένοις, οὔ μοι μέλει· μέλει δὲ ὅμως καὶ οὕτως· »τὴν γὰρ μετάνοιαν τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ μᾶλλον ἢ τὸν θάνατον αἱρεῖται.« »ἢν δὲ εἰσακούσητέ μου, τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς γῆς φάγεσθε«, ὁ παιδαγωγὸς πάλιν λέγει, γῆς ἀγαθὰ τὰ ἀνθρώπεια ὀνομάζων καλά, τὸ κάλλος, τὸν πλοῦτον, τὴν ὑγίειαν καὶ τὴν ἰσχύν, τὴν τροφήν· ἀγαθὰ μὲν γὰρ ὄντως »ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνέβη ποτέ«, περὶ τὸν ὄντως ὄντα βασιλέα τὰ ὄντως ὄντα ἀγαθὰ ὄντα καὶ ἀναμένοντα ἡμᾶς· ἀγαθῶν γάρ ἐστι καὶ δοτὴρ καὶ φύλαξ· κατὰ μετουσίαν δὲ ἐκείνων τὰ τῇδε συνωνυμεῖ, παιδαγωγοῦντος ἐνθέως τοῦ λόγου τὴν ἀνθρώπων ἀσθένειαν ἀπὸ τῶν αἰσθητῶν ἐπὶ τὴν νόησιν.
pass_a_gloss: I would advise even those who are married to love their wives at home not as servants face to face. For neither does Aristotle ever allow slaves to be joked with, and it is necessary for the wife to appear to be fond of her husband in their sight. But it is better for those who have begun from marriage to show dignity at home. For the greatest marriage of chastity breathes pure pleasure. The tragedy says wonderfully, Alas, alas, women, as if neither gold nor tyranny nor wealth's indulgence had as many different pleasures among people as the opinion of a good man and a pious woman, a just and manly-thinking mind. These are the commands of justice, and they must not be rejected, even if they have been spoken by those who possess worldly wisdom. Therefore, knowing each one's work, conduct your time of sojourning in fear, knowing that we were redeemed from our useless conduct, handed down from our fathers, not with perishable things, silver or gold, but with precious blood, as of a blameless and spotless lamb, Christ. Peter says, The past time is enough to have done the will of the Gentiles, having walked in lasciviousness, desires, wine-drinkings, revelings, drinkings, and lawless idolatries. Let us have the cross of the Lord as a boundary, by which we are crucified and surrounded by our former sins. Therefore, having been reborn, let us be fixed in the truth and let us be raised and sanctified, because the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are for their prayer, and the face of the Lord is against those who do evil. And who will harm us if we become zealous for the good? The best guidance is orderliness, being complete modesty and established power, the subsequent things being well-disposed to each other, working in a good deed, unbeaten in virtue. If I have spoken more roughly, managing the salvation of the correction, it has been spoken to me, says the Pedagogue, since he who reproves with frankness makes peace. If you listen to me, you will be saved; if you do not pay attention to what has been said, I do not care; yet I do care: the repentance of the sinner is chosen rather than death. If you listen to me, you will eat the good things of the earth, says the Pedagogue again, calling human goods good, beauty, wealth, health, and strength, nourishment; for the things that are truly good are those which neither ear has heard nor has arisen in the heart, concerning the truly existing King, the truly existing good things being and waiting for us; for He is the giver and guardian of good things; but the things that are named similarly here are according to a change of those things, the Word guiding human weakness from the senses to the intellect.

The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are for their prayer

pass_b_english: I would advise even married men to treat their wives with dignity at home, not as servants face to face. Aristotle himself never permitted slaves to be joked with; how much more, then, must a wife appear affectionate toward her husband in their presence. It is better for those who begin from marriage to show dignity at home. The supreme union of chastity breathes forth pure pleasure. Tragedy puts it wonderfully: "Alas, alas, women! As if neither gold, nor tyranny, nor the indulgence of wealth could differentiate human pleasures as much as the judgment of a good man and a pious woman — a mind that is just and thinks rightly." These are the commands of justice, and they must not be rejected even when spoken by those who possess worldly wisdom.

Therefore, knowing each person's work, conduct the time of your sojourn in fear, knowing that you were redeemed from your futile conduct handed down from your fathers, not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot (1 Peter 1:18–19). Peter says, "The time that has passed is enough for doing the will of the Gentiles, having walked in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry" (1 Peter 4:3). Let us make the cross of the Lord our boundary, by which we are crucified and hemmed in against our former sins. Having been born again, let us cleave to the truth; let us become sober and be sanctified, "for the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil" (1 Peter 3:12). And who will harm us if we become zealous for what is good?

The best training is orderliness — complete decorum and established power, with each subsequent duty fitting well with the next, working toward good deeds, unsurpassed in virtue. If I have spoken somewhat roughly, managing the salvation of correction, these words were spoken to me, says the Pedagogue, since "the one who reproves with frankness makes peace." If you listen to me, you will be saved; if you do not pay attention to what has been said, it is no concern of mine — yet I do care, even so, for "the repentance of the sinner is chosen rather than death." "If you listen to me, you shall eat the good things of the earth," the Pedagogue says again, calling human goods good — beauty, wealth, health, strength, and nourishment; for truly good things are "what no ear has heard, nor has entered the human heart," concerning the truly existing King, the truly existing good things that exist and await us; for He is both giver and guardian of good things. But the things here named similarly are by a change of those things, the Word guiding human weakness from the senses to the intellect.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the nuances of the Aristotle reference and the distinction between the 'truly existing King' and earthly goods. Scripture citations (1 Peter 1:18–19, 1 Peter 4:3, 1 Peter 3:12) are correctly added to the English text to identify the quoted/alluded passages as required. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek.
